correctness.rationale: The third-coordinate two-step closure forces opposite y-values, and b>0, k<1 force x0<0<x1. Both first-coordinate updates then give x0=-t and x1=1. The second-coordinate equations reduce every two-cycle to sin z=(b-1)/k and t(1+k sin(z+t))=b. Inside the sine wedge b<=1+k, a global a priori bound t<=b/(1-k) and (1-k)g'(t)>=1-3k>0 show exactly one positive amplitude per phase. The sine equation gives the exhaustive orbit counts modulo 2π and no fixed points exist. At b=1 the exact product of the displayed two Jacobians yields simple roots 1,(1±i√3)/2 at k=0; their first perturbation coefficients give a sink for phase π and repeller for phase 0 when k>0 is small. The standalone finite checker returned 640 consistency checks; infinite claims follow from these algebraic/inequality arguments, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The originating no-equilibria map was motivated by numerically observed hidden periodic attractors, making exact existence and stability of the simplest nontrivial periods a natural structural question. The theorem gives an exhaustive three-way b–k phase boundary, a unique amplitude for every permitted phase, and an analytically proved sink–repeller coexistence on an open parameter set. These facts cannot be read off numerical bifurcation plots, establish nonlinear-system dynamics in the previously unclassified weak-coupling regime, and distinguish two discrete phase branches by their full three-dimensional return multipliers. The k<1/3 monotonicity domain is openly stated as sufficient rather than falsely sharp.
